answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can cap each identity's workload by earned reputation, not by account count. Like a jetty that admits one boat at a time, the system grants transaction quotas only after an identity completes verified work: each agent must first finish peer-audited tasks, and its quota grows slowly with a clean record. Juniper cannot shortcut this by spawning clones, because every clone starts at zero and must independently pay the same time and compute cost. A knoll of fake identities gains no extra throughput, while misbehavior burns the attacker's accumulated standing.
